h1: The 5 Best Lawn Mowers Under $300 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Lawn Mowers Under $300 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five lawn mowers under $300, from 18-inch gas and cordless to manual reel models, with advice on which fits your yard.
summary: The PowerSmart EasyCut 18 inch gas mower is the best lawn mower under $300: a 144cc engine, five cutting heights and no battery limit. The Wild Badger 40V brushless is the cordless option for small yards, and the LawnMaster reel suits tiny, flat lawns kept short. The American Lawn Mower 14 inch reel is the cheapest.
intro: A cheap mower seldom fails for lack of power. It fails because the buyer matched the wrong type to the yard: a reel on thick grass, a narrow deck on a big lot, or a battery mower with no plan for a second pack. At this price the mismatch is the expensive part, because the mower ends up in the shed and the lawn goes uncut.

We ranked five mowers that sit well below the $300 ceiling, using the spec sheet and the way owners describe them. Cutting width, power source, upkeep and how much work each asks of you drove the order, since those factors decide whether a budget mower feels like a bargain or a chore. Rated width and engine size mattered more than brand names at this level.

products.name: PowerSmart EasyCut 18-Inch Gas Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Gas-mower cutting width at a price that leaves room in the budget.
products.description:
The PowerSmart EasyCut is an 18 inch gas mower with a 144cc four-cycle engine, side discharge, a five-position height adjustment and a price in the $100 to $200 range. A gas engine has no runtime cap, so a thick or tall stretch of grass never ends your afternoon halfway through. Five heights let you raise the deck after a long gap.

It ranks first because it combines full-width gas power with a low price. The Wild Badger removes fuel hassle but caps runtime, and the reel mowers cannot handle thick grass.

Buy it for a small to medium yard where finishing in a single pass matters. The caveats are fuel and oil upkeep, and noise. Skip it if you do not want to handle fuel or engine maintenance.
products.idealFor: Small to medium yards where finishing in one pass matters.
products.skipIf: You do not want to handle fuel or engine maintenance.

products.name: PowerSmart 18-Inch 144cc Gas Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Same class of mower as the top pick when that model is out of stock.
products.description:
The PowerSmart 18 inch 144cc gas mower is a push model with side discharge, in the same price bucket and engine class as the EasyCut. It is a stand-in for the top pick, with the same width and a simple push drive.

It ranks second because it lists no height range, and little separates it from the EasyCut except the missing detail. Think of it as the same class when the top model is out of stock.

Buy it if the EasyCut is unavailable and you want gas power at an 18 inch width. Skip it if you want a self-propelled drive or a mulching setup. Because the listing is thin, check for height positions and warranty details before ordering.
products.idealFor: Anyone wanting the top pick's class when it is out of stock.
products.skipIf: You want self-propelled drive or a mulching setup.

products.name: Wild Badger Power 40V 18-Inch Brushless Cordless Lawn Mower
products.verdict: Gas-width deck with none of the fuel or cord hassle.
products.description:
The Wild Badger Power is an 18 inch cordless mower with a 40V brushless motor, battery power and no cord or fuel. A brushless motor wears less than a brushed one and runs cooler, so it should hold up through years of weekly cuts. It is quiet enough for early morning mowing.

It ranks third because the battery limits runtime and thus lawn size, and a replacement battery later costs real money. It beats the gas models on noise and upkeep.

Buy it for a small to medium yard where quiet and low upkeep matter. Skip it if your lawn is large or the grass is thick and tall. For anything beyond small, plan on a second battery.
products.idealFor: Small to medium yards where quiet, low-upkeep mowing matters.
products.skipIf: Your lawn is large or the grass is thick and tall.

products.name: LawnMaster LMRM1602 16-Inch 5-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: A manual reel with a wider cut and zero running costs.
products.description:
The LawnMaster LMRM1602 is a 16 inch push reel mower with five blades, no fuel, no cord and no battery. A reel mower cuts like scissors, trimming blades against a fixed bed knife, which gives a clean cut on short grass and almost no noise.

It ranks fourth because it struggles with tall grass and demands all the effort from you. Its 16 inch width beats the American Lawn Mower's 14 inches, and the cost to run is zero.

Buy it for a small, flat lawn you mow often and keep short. Skip it if grass gets long between mows or the yard is bumpy. A reel stalls on tall stems, so cut frequently.
products.idealFor: Small flat lawns mowed often and kept short.
products.skipIf: Your grass gets long between mows or the yard is bumpy.

products.name: American Lawn Mower 1204-14 14-Inch 4-Blade Push Reel Mower
products.verdict: The simplest, lowest-cost way to keep a tiny lawn trimmed.
products.description:
The American Lawn Mower 1204-14 is a 14 inch four-blade push reel mower with no fuel, cord or battery, in the $50 to $100 bucket. It stores in a small space and needs almost no maintenance, which suits a tiny yard.

It ranks last because the 14 inch deck is the narrowest here and cannot handle tall grass. The LawnMaster covers two more inches per pass.

Buy it for a tiny flat lawn on the lowest budget. Skip it if you have more than a small patch of grass. Plan to mow often, since a reel works only on short grass.
products.idealFor: Tiny flat lawns and buyers who want the lowest cost.
products.skipIf: You have more than a small patch of grass.

whatMatters.detail: Deck width is how much grass you cut per pass. An 18 inch deck finishes a lawn faster than a 14 inch one, and the gap adds up over a season. Check the inch figure in the title and compare it against your lawn size, measured in rough minutes of mowing. A narrow deck on a big lot means many extra passes and lost time.

Gas gives unlimited runtime, battery gives quiet and no fuel, and a reel needs only your effort. Each suits a different yard. Look for engine cc or battery voltage in the listing, such as the 144cc on the PowerSmart models or 40V on the Wild Badger, and ask whether the runtime fits your lawn size before you pay.

Height positions let you raise the deck after a long gap and lower it later. This prevents scalping the lawn, which stresses grass and invites weeds. Look for a stated number of positions in the title or specs. The EasyCut lists five, while the second PowerSmart gives no range and the reel mowers adjust differently.

Gas engines need oil and fuel, batteries age, and reel blades need occasional adjustment. This ongoing cost matters more than the sticker price. Check what the listing says is included, and think about whether you will actually do the upkeep. A mower you neglect will cost more than one you can maintain easily.

Reel mowers suit small, flat, regularly cut lawns. Larger or rougher yards need a motor. Measure your lawn before you buy, and walk it for bumps and slopes. A bumpy lawn defeats a reel's fixed blades, while tall grass defeats it entirely, so be realistic about how often you will mow in the growing season.

faq.q: Can a reel mower handle thick grass?
faq.a: Not well. Reel mowers cut best when grass is kept short and mowed often. If your lawn grows quickly, the PowerSmart gas models are a better fit, and they take thick grass in stride without a battery to worry about.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake with a budget mower?
faq.a: Buying a narrow deck for a large yard. Every inch of width saves passes, so match the deck to the lawn. The 14 inch American Lawn Mower suits only tiny patches, and even the 16 inch LawnMaster is small.

faq.q: Is gas still worth it over battery?
faq.a: For bigger or tougher lawns, yes, because there is no runtime cap. Battery makes sense for small yards and quiet streets, as with the Wild Badger 40V, which has no fuel and runs quietly.
Most arrive partly assembled and need handle setup. Check the listing for what is included before buying, and keep the manual for the first fuel fill on the PowerSmart, since oil is needed too.

faq.q: How do I maintain a reel mower?
faq.a: Keep the blades clean and occasionally adjust the blade contact. There is no fuel, oil or spark plug to deal with, which is the main appeal of the LawnMaster and the American Lawn Mower, plus easy storage.

faq.q: Will a cordless mower cover my whole lawn?
faq.a: That depends on lawn size and battery capacity. If the lawn is bigger than small, plan for a second battery or pick a gas model such as the PowerSmart EasyCut, which avoids the issue.

finalTake: The PowerSmart EasyCut is the right mower under $300 for most yards, because gas power and an 18 inch deck get the job done in one pass. Choose the Wild Badger 40V for quiet cordless mowing on small lawns, and a reel only for tiny, flat ones. Match the type to the grass first.
